source.review_note: Approved exact 2022 engine access, top-end bench and commissioning operations composed with explicit handoffs and cold pressure-tester attachment before first oil-flow start. Independent composition review pending.

title: Rebuild the top end and reassemble the bike
completeness: Assembled-bike access, measured piston/cylinder and retained-head top-end service, refit, head-gasket pressure test and replacement-part break-in/post-maintenance. Documented oil-check-bolt closure and actual specialist/post-maintenance work remain explicit dependencies. Lower-engine and suspension internals are outside this route.

applicability.included: Exact stock US 2022 YZ450F with accepted retained cases, lower drives, head/caps and ECU/coil mountings; optional source-reviewed guide/valve and piston/cylinder renewal.
excluded: Wheel/frame/suspension bearing service or structural repair
Complete cable replacement or throttle-body sensor/calibration work
Broken chain, failed rear brake or seized sprocket nut preventing the reviewed manual holding method
ECU mounting-fastener service: source table3.8Nm conflicts with exploded8Nm; retained mounts are not disturbed.
Oil-level check-bolt torque/seal prescription: documented exact-interface closure required before work.
Head resurfacing, cylinder rebore/replate, aftermarket parts or ring filing
Lower timing-chain drive replacement, bottom-end overhaul or lubrication-fault diagnosis
Lower-engine crankcase, gearbox, oil-pump and clutch internal repair

prerequisites: Before beginning, obtain and record a documented exact2022 oil-level check-bolt refit torque/seal requirement from an attributed source or qualified Yamaha service provider. The manual requires opening it for final level but does not defensibly identify its closure torque; no generic cover or pressure-check bolt value is adopted.
Confirm exact stock engine, intact chain and working rear brake. Photograph all routing, shim positions and control settings.
Independent chassis, engine, swingarm and shock support is required. Lower shock and frame-side connecting-arm bolts are released for exhaust clearance; keep the remaining joints assembled.

ECU and ignition coil stay mounted on the aircase. Confirm the complete retained assembly can be lifted after disconnecting its identified couplers and plug cap without blocking the three case bolts or loading wiring. If actual clearance requires ECU removal, resolve its conflicting source torque first.
Any separate internal bench work must return sealed covers/filter/strainer and documented timing, clearances, lubrication and free rotation. No internals are serviced here.
Read the scope and arrange refit/commissioning before teardown.
Have exact diagrams available for head/cam order, timing, guide height and ring-gap orientation.
For guide renewal, arrange actual specialist seat refacing and separate new lapping/running valves.
Confirm measuring tools, new seals/gaskets and specified lubricants are available.
Have original illustrated manual and torque-check sheet available.
Arrange qualified assessment for required inaccessible checks or checks outside operator capability.
Do not record work as completed unless physically performed.
Have verified exact oil-check-bolt fastening and seal closure information before starting; do not substitute a nearby cover torque.
This route performs the replacement-head-gasket pressure test with the approved cold-attachment method before the first oil-flow start; actual adapter fit must be confirmed.
Plan required specialist seat work, tank-interior cleaning and inaccessible post-maintenance inspections before teardown; only actually completed work satisfies these records.

steps.title: Record the engine and job condition
steps.instruction: Record the exact stock engine identity, running condition and reason for removal. Photograph hose, electrical and bracket routing before access. Prepare an independently supported engine bench and a controlled lift with a helper; this guide removes/installs the assembly and does not repair its internals. Record initial clutch lever free play 7-12 mm and control condition before removing any cable end. Record the exact oil-level check-bolt closure document, applicable fastener/seal and torque before proceeding; this value is not established by the available manual.
verification: Exact bike, bench/supports, routing, initial7-12mm clutch free play and external check-bolt closure document recorded.

steps.title: Record the original cable positions
steps.instruction: Record pull/return cable positions at the grip against the exact handlebar diagram and actual grip free play, specified3-6mm. Preserve routing and adjustment without swapping cables.
verification: Original cable positions and actual free play recorded.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil before lifting
steps.instruction: For a normally running engine, warm for several minutes, stop and wait about5minutes; do not run a faulted engine solely to warm oil. Stand upright on level ground. Remove filler cap and the single drain bolt over a container. Leave filter/strainer assembled unless separately serviced. Drain completely and refit the drain with a new gasket at20Nm. Mark the engine empty.
verification: One drain closed with new gasket20Nm; engine marked empty.

steps.title: Prepare the bike
steps.instruction: Stop the engine, let it cool and support the bike. Clean the intake and fuel work area. Keep dirt out of open joints and fuel work away from ignition sources.
verification: Cold engine; stable bike; clean work area; parts/tools ready.

steps.title: Open the sub-seat
steps.instruction: Lift the fuel-tank-cap cover with fingers under both sides, upward toward the rear as illustrated; retain its plastic-band attachment to the seat. Open cap, transfer fuel to an appropriate container with fuel-safe equipment, then secure cap.
verification: Cap cover released intact; fuel safely contained and cap secured.

steps.title: Remove access panels
steps.instruction: Remove the left side-cover fasteners first, then the seat fasteners and slide the seat rearward with its attached cap cover. Remove the right side cover by releasing its illustrated projections from the slots. Label collars and fastener positions.
verification: Both covers and seat removed without damaging projections or plastic band.

steps.title: Isolate the battery
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, disconnect the negative battery lead first, then the positive lead. Insulate the loose terminals. Retain the battery and relay in place unless separate frame work requires removal; no starter action is allowed during the work.
verification: Negative then positive disconnected and insulated.

steps.title: Expose the tank
steps.instruction: Loosen the air-filter-cover quick-fastener screw. Release its two ribs from the air-scoop projections and slide the cover forward. Keep the filter installed. Remove left/right air scoops, releasing their illustrated projections, grooves and slots without prying. Retain collars.
verification: Forward cover removal and scoop locators preserved; filter remains sealed.

steps.title: Disconnect the tank
steps.instruction: Unplug the fuel-pump connector. Put cloths below and around the fuel-hose joint for residual pressure. Remove the connector holder, slide the cover back, press its two release buttons and separate the joint by hand. Fit the supplied joint covers to both openings immediately.
verification: Pump disconnected; both fuel openings capped; no forced hose tools.

steps.title: Lift the tank clear
steps.instruction: Remove the tank mounting fasteners, retaining the collars/dampers in their original locations, and lift the tank away. Support it so its weight does not rest on the fuel-pump mounting surface. Leave the pump installed in the tank.
verification: Tank supported; mounts accounted for; pump untouched.

steps.title: Release the intact case
steps.instruction: Label and unplug ECU and ignition-coil couplers, disconnect intake-temperature coupler and pull the plug cap clear without removing the spark plug. Leave ECU and coil bolted to the aircase. Release only the routing clips needed to free their leads. Loosen case joint clamp and remove its three mounting bolts with original collars/washers/dampers. Do not disturb the ECU bolts because the manual gives conflicting tightening values.
verification: Retained ECU/coil assembly disconnected from harness and plug; case bolts/clamp accessible without disturbing ECU mounts.

steps.title: Lift off and protect the intake
steps.instruction: Lift the complete aircase with retained ECU, coil and filter off the intake joint, supporting its high-tension lead and plug cap. Stop if a mount is inaccessible or the retained assembly cannot clear freely; do not force it or remove ECU mounts without resolving their torque conflict. Cover exposed intake and keep the removed assembly clean.
verification: Case/ECU/coil clear and supported; inlet protected; all retained mounts unchanged.

steps.title: Open the cable housing
steps.instruction: Pull back the rubber cover. Remove the housing screws and separate the throttle cable housing without pulling on the cables.
verification: Housing open; rubber cover and screws retained.

steps.title: Release the two grip-end cables
steps.instruction: Disengage the pull and return cable ends from their original seats in the throttle tube as shown. Support the cables without kinking them and withdraw the complete grip/tube assembly from the bar. Do not peel the bonded rubber grip off its tube or disturb the cable ends at the throttle body.
verification: Both identified ends released; intact grip/tube retained.

steps.title: Check the released parts
steps.instruction: Inspect the tube sliding surface and cable-end seats for damage and check that the cables move without binding. Keep dirt out of the open housing. A damaged or frayed cable needs a separate full cable-renewal operation before this access job can return to service.
verification: Retained parts accepted; no damaged cable or binding.

steps.title: Support suspension and open the exhaust clearance path
steps.instruction: Support chassis, swingarm/rear wheel and shock independently so neither released joint carries spring or bike load. Remove the shock lower bolt and connecting-arm frame-side bolt as the exhaust prerequisites require. Preserve collars/seals and support the arm/shock without hanging from the remaining joints. Keep upper shock and other linkage pivots assembled.
verification: Two required access bolts removed under support; collars/seals retained; other joints untouched.

steps.title: Remove the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Support the silencer. Loosen its joint clamp, remove its two mounting bolts and lift the complete silencer off its joint. Keep the silencer body, end cap and packing assembled.
verification: Complete silencer supported and removed; internals untouched.

steps.title: Remove the intermediate pipe
steps.instruction: Loosen pipe2 joint clamp and remove its bracket bolt while supporting the pipe. With the shock lower and frame-side connecting-arm joints already released, move pipe2 through the exact illustrated clearance path and remove without forcing adjacent parts.
verification: Exhaust2 clear without load on unsupported suspension or hoses.

steps.title: Remove the header and old seals
steps.instruction: Remove the header nuts and header pipe. Leave the header protector attached. Remove the old exhaust-port gasket at the cylinder head and the two pipe-joint gaskets; inspect joint faces and supports for damage before refitting.
verification: Header removed; all three separated joint seals identified; protector untouched.

steps.title: Set up for a cold drain
steps.instruction: Stand the cooled bike upright on a level surface. Place the collection container beneath the engine and position it close to the drain outlet, because flow can shoot sideways when the radiator cap is released.
verification: Bike stable; engine and coolant cold; collection ready.

steps.title: Open the drain and radiator cap
steps.instruction: Remove the coolant drain bolt and its copper washer. Place a thick cloth over the radiator cap and turn it slowly counterclockwise toward its detent to release residual pressure. Once hissing stops, press down and turn farther to remove the cap. Let the coolant drain into the container. Thoroughly flush the cooling system with clean tap water as Yamaha directs, then drain the flush water completely before fitting the new drain washer. Account for residual water when establishing the final coolant mixture.
verification: Drain complete; old washer removed; cap opened only when cold.

steps.title: Install a new drain washer
steps.instruction: Install a new copper washer and the coolant drain bolt. Tighten the bolt to 10 N·m.
verification: New washer installed; drain bolt 10 N·m.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Identify radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 from the source drawing. Mark each hose and clamp position, loosen its engine-side clamp and release the hoses from the engine. Keep radiators mounted and protect the open hose/engine ports from dirt. Do not remove coolant pipe joints or the temperature sensor itself.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 labeled and clear; pipe joints/sensor remain sealed.

steps.title: Lift the intact throttle body from the engine joint
steps.instruction: Label/disconnect injector, intake-pressure and throttle-position sensor couplers. Keep sensors installed. Clean lower joint, loosen clamp and lift intact throttle body clear. Support its detached grip-end cables without tension; body-end seats, screws and pulley stay untouched. Cover engine inlet and body openings; never push the throttle valve.
verification: Three identified sensor/injector couplers disconnected; complete body/cables separately supported; calibration untouched.

steps.title: Disconnect the left engine harness interfaces
steps.instruction: Release only the retaining clips/ties needed to free engine leads. Disconnect the stator, crankshaft-position and gear-position connectors; keep the gear-position switch bolted to the engine so its seal is not disturbed. Match connector identity to the diagrams, using the actual labeled connectors and exact source routing. Label and protect both halves.
verification: Stator/crank-position/gear-position leads released; sensor seals untouched.

steps.title: Disconnect starter, ground and plug interfaces
steps.instruction: Disconnect coolant-temperature coupler and remove the head ground terminal bolt. Plug cap was released with the retained aircase group. At the starter lead pull back its rubber terminal cover and hold the motor-side nut with a spanner while undoing the lead nut. Release necessary lead clips and support harness clear. Leave motor and rigid motor covers installed; if terminal access is blocked, do not force it.
verification: Ground, temperature and starter lead free; isolated battery; motor/covers retained.

steps.title: Remove chain, sprocket and shift pedal
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel still secured, chain intact and rear brake still fully mounted, select neutral. Remove the sprocket cover and retained drive-chain guide, label their arrangement, and flatten the old lock-washer tabs. Have a helper hold the rear brake firmly while using a correctly fitting socket and manual breaker bar to loosen the sprocket nut, following the attributed Nick Dole technique. Do not use impact, heat or jam the chain against the case. Once loose, release the stock chain joint and remove the chain, retaining its matched link/plate and preparing a new clip. Remove the nut, old lock washer and sprocket. Mark and remove the shift pedal, preserving punch-mark alignment.
verification: Chain and sprocket clear; old lock washer/clip retired; shift position recorded.

source_links.title: Nick Dole manual rear-brake holding technique

steps.title: Disconnect and record the cable clutch
steps.instruction: Record clutch lever free play and the cable-end/adjuster positions. Release cable tension with the handlebar adjuster as necessary. Disconnect the engine-end cable nipple from the push lever and release the cable outer from its bracket as shown in the inset; keep the push lever, shaft and clutch cover installed. Retain the cable with its handlebar lever and support it clear of the engine lifting path. This bike has a cable clutch.
verification: Engine-end nipple and outer detached and identified; push lever and clutch internals remain installed; cable supported.

steps.title: Clear pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard, brake-pedal pivot bolt and return spring. Support the pedal with its master-cylinder linkage attached. Label and release the cylinder-head breather hose from the engine and its routing holders. Keep brake hydraulics closed.
verification: Guard/pedal/spring retained; breather clear; brake system closed.

steps.title: Support engine and swingarm before undoing mounts
steps.instruction: Support the engine independently. Support the swingarm and prepare a same-diameter temporary support shaft from its other side if needed when the pivot is withdrawn. Confirm every electrical connector, hose, intake assembly and cable is clear before loosening the engine mounts.
verification: Independent supports ready; all engine interfaces clear.

steps.title: Release the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove both upper brackets and the two lower brackets with four identified shims and their mapped hardware. Preserve left/right shim positions. Withdraw the pivot while maintaining swingarm support with the temporary shaft. Keep the engine independently supported until every mount is free.
verification: Two lower brackets/four shims identified; shared pivot removed once with swingarm supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out to the right
steps.instruction: Lift the engine and move its lower part toward the right side of the chassis as shown in the OEM drawing, then transfer it to the prepared support. Stop if any interface catches. Keep the inlet, exhaust and fluid ports protected from contamination.
verification: Assembly removed to right; no trapped interface; engine stable.

steps.title: Confirm the engine is ready for bench work
steps.instruction: Confirm exact standard US 2022 YZ450F stock engine, cold at room temperature, drained and securely supported after the preceding engine-removal steps. Intake, exhaust, coolant and electrical interfaces must be clear. Retain assembled crankcases, clutch, gearbox, starter, generator and oil-pump systems. Plan the head repair and later installation/commissioning before opening the engine.
verification: Engine identity, condition and access handoff recorded.
steps.composition_adaptation: Continuous-route bench entry after its own engine removal.

steps.title: Expose the valve train
steps.instruction: Clean around the plug before removing it. Disconnect the head breather and remove plug, head-cover bolts, cover, top chain guide and old cover/plug-hole gaskets. Keep the breather plate and its mounts intact. Protect the open engine from dirt.
verification: Cover hardware and top guide retained; sealing surfaces protected.

steps.title: Open the timing inspection ports
steps.instruction: Remove the timing-mark and crankshaft-end access screws and their O-rings. Keep their identities separate.
verification: Both ports open; screws identified.

steps.title: Set the cold measurement position
steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise by hand. Align the rotor TDC mark with the cover mark and verify both cam-sprocket marks align with the cam-cap surface edges in the diagram. Do not force resistance or rely on the rotor mark alone.
verification: Rotor and both cam marks recorded.

steps.title: Measure the four valve clearances
steps.instruction: Use a feeler gauge at each illustrated cam/lifter gap with the engine cold at room temperature and piston at the confirmed TDC position. Record intake left/right and exhaust left/right. Intake is 0.10–0.17 mm; exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm. These readings establish the pre-repair condition, not final acceptance.
verification: All four cold readings and positions saved.

steps.title: Remove the chain tensioner
steps.instruction: Remove the tensioner cap bolt, tensioner mounting bolts, tensioner and gaskets. Retain the chain position; keep the crank at the established position.
verification: Tensioner removed and sealing pieces identified.

steps.title: Lift out the cams
steps.instruction: Loosen cap bolts evenly in a crisscross pattern from outside inward, then remove caps and cams. Label intake/exhaust, caps, dowels and hardware. Wire the chain securely so it cannot fall into the crankcase. Do not turn the crank with the cams being removed. Account for and retain the two illustrated cam retaining clips without dropping them into the chain cavity.
verification: Cams/caps kept in matched positions; chain supported.

steps.title: Inspect the tensioner
steps.instruction: Reject cracks or damage. With light finger pressure on the rod, use a thin screwdriver to wind it fully clockwise. Release the screwdriver while maintaining light pressure: the rod must extend smoothly. Replace the complete tensioner if it fails.
verification: Condition and smooth-extension result recorded.

steps.title: Release and lift the head
steps.instruction: Use the removal diagram on this page, which is different from the tightening numbering. Loosen each bolt half a turn per pass in illustrated order 1–6 until all are loose, then remove them. The two small bolts are M6×35 mm and four main bolts M10×149 mm. Lift the head, retain dowels and intake-side chain guide, and remove the head gasket while keeping the chain supported. Leave head studs and oil-passage plugs installed.
verification: Head removed; removal order followed and chain retained.

steps.title: Inspect the head and intake chain guide
steps.instruction: Remove carbon with a rounded scraper, avoiding plug threads and sealing faces; remove deposits/rust from coolant passages. Inspect head damage/scratches and guide wear/damage; replace a damaged guide. Measure head warpage with straightedge and feeler gauge across the illustrated directions: limit 0.05 mm. This route retains a sound original head and excludes resurfacing or replacement of a damaged head.
verification: Warpage readings, head condition and chain-guide disposition saved.

steps.title: Lift off the cylinder
steps.instruction: Remove the cylinder bolt, lift the cylinder while retaining chain/guide through its cavity, and collect the base gasket and two dowels. Support the exposed piston and cover the crankcase opening.
verification: Cylinder removed and crankcase opening protected.

steps.title: Remove piston and rings
steps.instruction: Cover the case opening before removing pin clips. Deburr the clip groove and pin bore area if needed; never hammer the pin. If it remains tight use the specified piston-pin puller. Remove pin and piston. Spread each ring only enough by hand to lift its opposite side over the crown, keeping top, second and oil rings identified.
verification: Piston/rings identified; no clip or debris lost.

steps.title: Measure the cylinder
steps.instruction: Inspect cylinder and piston walls for vertical scratches. Measure side-to-side and front-to-back at the three illustrated heights, recording D1–D6; C is their maximum. Standard bore 97.000–97.010 mm, wear limit 97.060 mm. Scratched walls require cylinder replacement and piston/rings as a set. This route supports exact stock replacement, not rebore or replating.
verification: Six bore readings and wall condition recorded.

steps.title: Measure piston diameter and actual clearance
steps.instruction: Measure piston diameter on the illustrated axis 9.0 mm above the skirt bottom: standard 96.955–96.970 mm. Calculate actual C minus piston diameter. The manual separately specifies 0.010–0.045 mm clearance and 0.15 mm limit. Preserve both stated ranges: individually acceptable diameters do not automatically establish an acceptable pair. Resolve a failing actual fit with the prescribed cylinder/piston/ring set replacement and remeasurement.
verification: Piston diameter, datum, actual subtraction and fit disposition saved.

steps.title: Measure ring side clearances
steps.instruction: Clean carbon from grooves and rings before measuring. Top standard side clearance is 0.015–0.065 mm, limit 0.120 mm; second standard is 0.020–0.060 mm, limit 0.100 mm. An out-of-specification result requires piston and rings as a set.
verification: Top and second side-clearance readings and parts decisions saved.

steps.title: Measure ring end gaps
steps.instruction: Square each ring near the cylinder bottom using the piston crown as illustrated. Record top and second end gaps: limits 0.55 mm and 0.85 mm respectively. Replace an out-of-specification ring. The oil expander gap is not measurable; if oil-rail gap is excessive replace the oil-ring set. No numerical oil-rail acceptance or ring filing amount is supplied here.
verification: Measured gaps and ring disposition saved; unresolved oil-rail condition not accepted by an invented limit.

steps.title: Inspect piston pin and bore
steps.instruction: A blue or grooved pin requires replacement and investigation of the lubrication system before this route can continue. Measure pin outside diameter (minimum 17.981 mm) and piston pin bore (maximum 18.045 mm). Replace pin or piston for the corresponding failed measurement. Also record the actual pin-to-bore clearance against the listed 0.004–0.024 mm range.
verification: Pin/bore measurements, actual clearance and surface condition saved.

steps.title: Accept the actual piston assembly
steps.instruction: Record the exact stock parts retained or renewed. All required cylinder, piston, ring and pin checks must pass on the final chosen parts before assembly. Do not treat wear limits as an invented new-part target or infer correct fit from catalog sizes. Lubrication faults, unidentified parts and unresolved measured fit stop this route.
verification: Final measured assembly and replacement decisions accepted.

steps.title: Identify each lifter and pad
steps.instruction: On the removed head, protect the chain opening with a cloth and use the valve lapper to lift each lifter and pad. Store and label all four pairs by original position. Keep the original cams and caps matched to this head.
verification: Four lifter/pad positions recorded.

steps.title: Check valve sealing before stripping
steps.instruction: Pour clean solvent into intake and exhaust ports as illustrated and check for leakage through each seat. The source identifies kerosene in its leakage check. Record leakage and inspect the associated face, seat and contact width; dispose of the solvent before further work.
verification: Four seat-sealing observations saved.

steps.title: Remove the valve assemblies
steps.instruction: Use the valve spring compressor and 22 mm attachment to compress each spring and remove its cotters. Release the compressor, then remove retainer, spring, valve, old stem seal and spring seat. Keep every part identified by valve position.
verification: All parts indexed and removed seals set aside for replacement.

steps.title: Inspect and measure valves and guides
steps.instruction: Measure each guide ID and stem OD and subtract to obtain actual clearance. Guide ID is 5.500–5.512 mm; minimum stem OD intake 5.445 mm/exhaust 5.435 mm. Clearance limits intake 0.080 mm/exhaust 0.100 mm. Inspect faces and stem ends; reject mushroomed ends. Measure stem runout on supports with a dial gauge: maximum 0.020 mm. Do not accept an undersize stem merely because clearance passes.
verification: Four ID/OD/clearance/runout results and condition decisions saved.

steps.title: Measure seat contact
steps.instruction: Remove carbon and inspect seats. Apply blue layout fluid to each valve face, press the valve through its guide against the seat, remove it and measure the contact band where blueing was displaced. Contact width limit is 1.5 mm for both intake and exhaust. Pitting/wear or failed original seat width requires head replacement under the inspection instructions and is outside this retained-head route.
verification: Four contact widths and seat condition saved.

steps.title: Inspect springs and lifters
steps.instruction: Measure spring free lengths: intake minimum 36.65 mm, exhaust minimum 35.55 mm. Replace failed springs with correct stock parts. Damaged or scratched lifters require lifters and cylinder head together; do not fit a fresh lifter into a failed head in this route.
verification: Spring measurements, lifter condition and decisions saved.

steps.title: Choose retained valves or guide renewal
steps.instruction: Continue into guide renewal only with a sound retained head, acceptable seats and lifters, appropriate replacement parts and arranged specialist seat refacing. A new running valve always requires a new guide; new valves used for lapping must be replaced by distinct new running valves. If all original valves/guides/seats passed and no lapping or machining is needed, choose the retained-valve branch instead.
verification: Repair path and component decisions recorded.

branches.label: Retain all four accepted original valves and guides
branches.condition: All original valve, guide, seat, sealing and lifter checks pass; no lapping or machining is required.

steps.title: Prepare the guide-renewal parts
steps.instruction: For every guide/valve position being renewed, identify the correct new guide, a new valve used only for lapping and a distinct new valve for running. Keep the running valves away from lapping compound. Preserve unaffected original parts only if their recorded checks passed. Arrange professional seat refacing; this guide does not specify cutter angles or a machining allowance.
verification: Renewal positions, separate lapping/running valves and refacing service recorded.

steps.title: Heat the head and remove the guides
steps.instruction: Heat the stripped head to 100 °C in an oven to preserve the guide fit. Support it securely and use the 5.5 mm guide remover in the illustrated direction to remove each selected guide. Handle the heated head with suitable protection.
verification: Head temperature and guides removed recorded.

steps.title: Install the new guides
steps.instruction: Use the illustrated 5.5 mm guide installer 90890-04015 / YM-04015 and remover to drive each new guide to its measured installation height from the shown head datum. Intake height 13.5–13.9 mm; exhaust 12.2–12.6 mm. Keep intake/exhaust locations distinct.
verification: Each guide height measured and recorded.

steps.title: Ream and measure the new guides
steps.instruction: Use the specified 5.5 mm reamer after installation. Measure actual guide ID, new running-valve stem OD and clearance for every renewed position. Apply the same 5.500–5.512 mm ID, intake/exhaust minimum stem diameters 5.445/5.435 mm and clearance limits 0.080/0.100 mm. Confirm the running valves also pass the 0.020 mm runout check; remove all machining debris.
verification: New guide/running-valve measurements and cleanliness accepted.

steps.title: Have the seats refaced for the new guides
steps.instruction: Have a qualified cylinder-head specialist reface every seat associated with a renewed guide before lapping. Record the actual completed service and resulting seat condition. Cutter selection, angles and material removal are not prescribed here; do not mark an arranged appointment as completed work.
verification: Actual specialist refacing record and accepted seat condition attached.

steps.title: Lap with the sacrificial new valves
steps.instruction: Use only the new lapping valves assigned to the renewed positions. Apply coarse compound to the face and molybdenum disulfide oil to the stem; keep compound out of the stem-to-guide gap. Insert the valve and turn it with the lapper, using the illustrated tap-and-lap action until contact is evenly polished. Remove all compound from face and seat.
verification: Coarse lapping completed without contaminating guides.

steps.title: Finish lapping and recheck contact
steps.instruction: Repeat with fine compound and clean all compound away after every lapping stage. Apply blue layout fluid, press the valve into its seat, remove and measure the contact band again. Maximum contact width is 1.5 mm. If contact remains out of specification, return for refacing and repeat the lapping/measurement sequence before proceeding.
verification: Final renewed-seat widths and contact accepted.

steps.title: Separate lapping valves from running parts
steps.instruction: Remove all sacrificial lapping valves from the running-parts tray. Use the distinct new running valves for renewed positions; do not install a valve used for lapping into the running engine. Clean the head and confirm the final running-valve/guide measurements remain accepted.
verification: Running-valve identities and discarded lapping valves recorded.

steps.title: Install valves and new stem seals
steps.instruction: Clean stem ends; lubricate stems and all new stem seals with molybdenum disulfide oil. Fit each spring seat, new stem seal, accepted valve, spring and retainer. Original retained parts return to their original positions; renewed parts go to their recorded positions. Install springs with the larger pitch upward.
verification: Four valve assemblies seated with new seals and correct spring orientation.

steps.title: Secure the cotters
steps.instruction: Compress each spring with the specified tool and 22 mm attachment and install its cotters. Release the tool, then lightly tap each valve tip with a soft-face hammer to seat the cotters. Excessive impact can damage the valve.
verification: Cotters seated in all four assemblies.

steps.title: Confirm final valve sealing
steps.instruction: Repeat the illustrated clean-solvent port check on the assembled head, including the actual new running valves where fitted. A leaking seat cannot proceed to engine assembly; resolve the seat/valve condition and repeat acceptance. After acceptance, drain the test solvent and dry the ports before engine assembly.
verification: Four final running-valve sealing results accepted.

steps.title: Return the pads and lifters
steps.instruction: Apply engine oil to pads and lifters, return each to its identified location and verify every lifter rotates smoothly with a finger. Preserve the pad numbers and original positions for final clearance adjustment.
verification: Four pads/lifters installed in their identified positions.

steps.title: Measure cam lobes
steps.instruction: Inspect for blue discoloration, pitting and scratches. Measure each lobe height on the illustrated axis: intake minimum 38.030 mm and exhaust minimum 34.170 mm. A failed cam needs replacement; this route continues only with accepted exact stock cams and a serviceable matching head/caps.
verification: Lobe readings and cam surface decisions saved.

steps.title: Measure the cam journals in the head
steps.instruction: Place cams in the head, position Plastigauge on the illustrated journals, install dowels and matching caps, and tighten caps crisscross from inner to outer at 10 N·m. Do not turn the cams during measurement. Remove caps evenly and read the flattened strips. Required clearance is 0.028–0.062 mm. Clean off the Plastigauge before final assembly.
verification: Journal-clearance readings recorded and measuring material removed.

steps.title: Resolve cam and chain defects
steps.instruction: If journal clearance failed, measure journal OD against 21.959–21.972 mm: a failed journal requires a cam, while an in-range journal with failed clearance requires head and caps together. Inspect chain for stiffness/damage and sprockets for more than one-quarter tooth wear; either condition requires chain and cam replacement as a set. Check smooth decompressor movement and projecting lever pin. This route does not remove the lower chain drive or replace the head/cap set; such failures require that repair before continuing.
verification: Cam, chain, sprocket and decompressor disposition accepted.

steps.title: Install the rings
steps.instruction: Install the oil expander, lower rail, upper rail, second ring and top ring in that order. Manufacturer marks or numbers face upward. Use the accepted matched parts from the measurement records.
verification: Ring order and markings confirmed.

steps.title: Fit piston, pin and new clips
steps.instruction: Oil the piston and pin with engine oil. Orient the piston mark toward the exhaust/rear of the engine. Protect the case opening while inserting pin and new clips. Fully seat the clips, keeping each clip end away from the piston cutout.
verification: Orientation and new clip seating confirmed.

steps.title: Set the ring-gap positions
steps.instruction: Oil piston, rings and cylinder. Match the five end-gap positions exactly to this diagram, including its 15° offsets: a top ring, b second ring, c upper oil rail, d expander, e lower oil rail. Use the piston drawing as the orientation reference rather than guessing clock positions.
verification: Five ring-gap positions checked against the diagram.

steps.title: Install the cylinder
steps.instruction: Account for and remove the crankcase protective cloth before lowering the cylinder, keeping the timing chain supported. Install new base gasket and dowels. Compress the rings by hand as the cylinder is lowered, passing the timing chain and exhaust-side guide through their cavity. Do not force a snagged ring. Tighten the cylinder bolt to 10 N·m.
verification: Cylinder seated without ring damage; bolt tightened.

steps.title: Seat the accepted head
steps.instruction: Confirm final piston fit, valve/head checks and selected repair are accepted. Install intake-side guide, dowels, new head gasket and head while drawing the chain upward. Match the gasket orientation to the illustration and keep passages clear.
verification: Head and new gasket correctly seated; chain retained.

steps.title: Prepare the main head bolts
steps.instruction: Wash bolt threads/contact surfaces, both washer contact faces, head contact faces and crankcase threads. Apply molybdenum disulfide grease to the four main-bolt threads/contact faces and both washer faces. Install washers and bolts, lightly seating them in the installation diagram order. Keep the small bolts distinct.
verification: Four main bolts and washers prepared as specified.

steps.title: Tighten the first stage
steps.instruction: Following installation diagram order 1–4, tighten the main bolts to 40 N·m in two or three stages. Do not use the removal-diagram numbering.
verification: All four main bolts initially tightened to 40 N·m in the illustrated order.

steps.title: Retighten one main bolt at a time
steps.instruction: Remove only installation bolt 1, without loosening any other. Reapply molybdenum disulfide grease to threads/contact face and both washer faces. Refit at 23 N·m, make reference marks and turn an additional 90°. Complete the same entire operation on bolts 2, 3 and 4 individually in order; finish each before loosening the next.
verification: Each main bolt individually regreased, tightened to 23 N·m and turned 90° before the next is loosened.

steps.title: Finish the head fastening
steps.instruction: In installation order 1–4 turn each main bolt a further 60°. Tighten the two small bolts at installation positions 5 and 6 to 10 N·m with clean, dry threads. The oil-passage plugs remain installed; their separate locking-agent arrows do not apply to these small head bolts.
verification: Final 60° on all four main bolts and 10 N·m on both small head bolts recorded.

steps.title: Set the cams at TDC
steps.instruction: Account for and remove all protective cloths from the head and timing-chain space before installing the cams. Turn the crank counterclockwise to align rotor TDC with the cover mark. Apply molybdenum disulfide oil to cams and engine oil to the decompressor. Fit chain onto both sprockets and set both cam marks at the cap-surface edges in the diagram. Do not rotate the crank while installing cams.
verification: Rotor/cam alignment recorded.

steps.title: Secure the cam caps
steps.instruction: Protect the head cavity while fitting both retained cam clips so neither can fall inside; account for and remove that cloth before continuing. Install matching caps and dowels. Oil bolt threads and contact surfaces. Tighten evenly to 10 N·m in two or three stages using the exact seven-bolt numbered sequence in the diagram.
verification: Both clips, matching caps and seven bolts seated; 10 N·m sequence recorded; protective cloth removed.

steps.title: Fit and release the tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the rod fully clockwise with light finger pressure. Fit new illustrated body/sealing gaskets, tensioner UP mark upward, and mounting bolts at 10 N·m. Release the screwdriver and confirm smooth rod extension, then install the new cap gasket and cap bolt at 6 N·m.
verification: Tensioner extended smoothly; gaskets and 10/6 N·m settings confirmed.

steps.title: Check timing by hand
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise several turns without forcing resistance. Return rotor TDC to the cover mark and verify both cam marks match the head/cap surfaces. Correct any mismatch before proceeding; never use the starter to test unresolved timing.
verification: Several-turn hand check and all timing marks accepted.

steps.title: Measure the final cold clearances
steps.instruction: At the confirmed TDC position and room temperature, record all four gaps using a feeler gauge. Intake 0.10–0.17 mm; exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm. Choose the next action from the actual readings; these results do not automatically approve closure.
verification: Four readings and required next action recorded.

steps.title: Choose adjustment or closure
steps.instruction: If all four cold readings are within specification, choose the close-up branch. Otherwise continue with the pad adjustment below using the actual current installed pad and measured gap. Unsupported pad selection or a component fault cannot be bypassed by selecting close-up.
verification: Reading-based path recorded.

branches.label: All four cold clearances pass — close the engine
branches.condition: All four latest cold readings are in range and all timing checks pass; no adjustment required.

steps.title: Reopen the cam and pad access
steps.instruction: At the confirmed TDC position remove tensioner cap, mounting bolts and tensioner. Loosen cap bolts evenly crisscross from outside inward, lift matching caps/cams and secure the chain. Lift each affected lifter/pad with the lapper, protecting the opening and preserving exact positions. Account for and retain the two illustrated cam retaining clips without dropping them into the chain cavity.
verification: Cams and affected pads removed without losing identity or chain position.

steps.title: Select each replacement pad from the correct chart
steps.instruction: Record the current installed pad number. Convert its last digit only as listed: 0/1/2 to 0; 4/5/6 to 5; 8/9 to the next ten (148 becomes 150). Digits 3 and 7 are unspecified. Use the intake chart or exhaust chart to intersect the measured cold-gap row with that pad column. Record the resulting pad number. Blank cells, unreadable numbers, unlisted digit conversions or readings between/outside chart rows require clarification, not extrapolation. Available stock pads are 1.20–2.40 mm in 0.05 mm increments.
verification: Each new pad traced to exact valve, current pad and chart cell.

steps.title: Install the selected pads
steps.instruction: Apply molybdenum disulfide oil to stem ends and engine oil to lifters. Fit correct selected pads with numbers up and original lifters in their original positions. Do not twist them forcibly; each lifter must rotate smoothly with a finger. After securing every pad and lifter, account for and remove the protective cloth from the timing-chain space before the next cam-installation step.
verification: Selected pads installed in recorded positions.

steps.title: Set the cams at TDC
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise to align rotor TDC with the cover mark. Apply molybdenum disulfide oil to cams and engine oil to the decompressor. Fit chain onto both sprockets and set both cam marks at the cap-surface edges in the diagram. Do not rotate the crank while installing cams.
verification: Rotor/cam alignment recorded.

steps.title: Secure the cam caps
steps.instruction: Protect the head cavity while fitting both retained cam clips so neither can fall inside; account for and remove that cloth before continuing. Install matching caps and dowels. Oil bolt threads and contact surfaces. Tighten evenly to 10 N·m in two or three stages using the exact seven-bolt numbered sequence in the diagram.
verification: Both clips, matching caps and seven bolts seated; 10 N·m sequence recorded; protective cloth removed.

steps.title: Fit and release the tensioner
steps.instruction: Wind the rod fully clockwise with light finger pressure. Fit new illustrated body/sealing gaskets, tensioner UP mark upward, and mounting bolts at 10 N·m. Release the screwdriver and confirm smooth rod extension, then install the new cap gasket and cap bolt at 6 N·m.
verification: Tensioner extended smoothly; gaskets and 10/6 N·m settings confirmed.

steps.title: Check timing by hand
steps.instruction: Turn the crank counterclockwise several turns without forcing resistance. Return rotor TDC to the cover mark and verify both cam marks match the head/cap surfaces. Correct any mismatch before proceeding; never use the starter to test unresolved timing.
verification: Several-turn hand check and all timing marks accepted.

steps.title: Measure the final cold clearances
steps.instruction: At the confirmed TDC position and room temperature, record all four gaps using a feeler gauge. Intake 0.10–0.17 mm; exhaust 0.15–0.22 mm. Choose the next action from the actual readings; these results do not automatically approve closure.
verification: Four readings and required next action recorded.

steps.title: Accept the adjusted clearances
steps.instruction: All four latest readings must now be within the cold specifications. If any fail, repeat the cam-removal, chart selection, installation, timing and measurement sequence before marking this step complete. Preserve every changed pad and final reading in the record; do not continue to the cover with failed clearance.
verification: All four final cold readings and timing accepted.

steps.title: Reseal the head cover
steps.instruction: Fit the top chain guide, new head-cover gasket and new plug-hole gasket. Apply ThreeBond 1215 / Yamaha bond No.1215 to the cover gasket as illustrated, install the cover and tighten its bolts to 10 N·m. Keep the retained breather plate intact.
verification: Guide and new gaskets seated; cover secured.

steps.title: Close plug and timing access
steps.instruction: Restore the head breather. Clean the spark plug and its gasket seat, install at 13 N·m and refit the cap when its engine interface is restored. Fit two new access-screw O-rings with lithium-soap-based grease, and tighten timing-mark screw to 6 N·m and crankshaft-end screw to 10 N·m.
verification: Plug, breather and both access ports closed with correct preparation.

steps.title: Verify the engine and rear bearing stacks
steps.instruction: Record the actual completed top-end work: installed parts, piston/cylinder/ring and valve/guide measurements, completed specialist seat work if used, accepted cold valve clearances, timing, lubrication and free rotation. Confirm top-end covers and access plugs are sealed and retained oil-filter closure accepted before refit. No unresolved bench fault may pass this handoff. Preserve the supported swingarm side stacks for the single pivot replacement.
verification: Actual top-end parts, measurements and timing accepted; covers/access plugs/filter closed; original swingarm side stacks supported.
steps.composition_adaptation: Replace standalone intact-engine handoff with the actual completed top-end repair records.

steps.title: Place the engine back in the chassis
steps.instruction: Bring supported engine in from the right, lower part first. Align mounts without trapping hoses or leads. Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the pivot shaft and insert from the right while withdrawing temporary support, preserving original swingarm side stacks. No lithium grease on pivot-nut threads is specified here.
verification: Engine and swingarm aligned; M-greased pivot from right; no newer-year nut preparation inherited.

steps.title: Install and secure the engine brackets
steps.instruction: Restore two lower brackets and four shims with shim projections toward the outside of the bike, plus both upper brackets and mapped hardware. Follow installation sequence: pivot nut85Nm; lower mount53Nm; front bracket bolts34Nm; front engine mount55Nm; upper bracket bolts34Nm; upper mounts45Nm. Keep the assembly supported/aligned throughout.
verification: Shim projections outward; recorded85/53/34/55/34/45Nm at exact labeled joints.

steps.title: Reconnect and adjust the cable clutch
steps.instruction: Restore the identified clutch cable outer to its engine bracket and nipple to the push lever as illustrated; tighten the engine-end cable locknut to 7 Nm if loosened. Verify full seating. Set lever free play to 7-12 mm using the handlebar adjuster first. If its range is insufficient, slide the cable cover, loosen the cable-side adjuster locknut, adjust and tighten that locknut to 4.3 Nm, then restore the cover. Check smooth clutch operation through both steering locks and record actual free play.
verification: Engine cable-end and outer fully seated; disturbed engine locknut 7 Nm; cable-side adjuster locknut 4.3 Nm if used; actual lever free play 7-12 mm recorded.

steps.title: Restore pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Install new pedal-pivot O-rings in both illustrated positions with lithium-soap grease. Grease pivot/seal contacts as shown and restore pivot bolt26Nm and return spring; engine guard7Nm. Restore head breather at engine and original holders: between radiator hose and engine bracket, outlet down aligned with lower down tube. Keep it clear of lower/front engine bosses and route radiator breather around it as illustrated.
verification: Two new LS pedal seals;26/7Nm; head breather points down in exact route, not into aircase.

steps.title: Restore the drive sprocket and chain
steps.instruction: Fit the original serviceable drive sprocket and new correct lock washer. Leave the nut hand-threaded temporarily; its final torque and tab locking are a later explicit step after rear-wheel, brake and chain closure. Align shift-shaft/pedal punch marks and tighten the pedal bolt to 12 Nm. With the supported rear wheel still installed, loosen the axle nut and both adjuster locknuts and back off adjusters enough to bring the wheel forward for chain installation. Fit the retained stock chain with matched link/plate and new clip, closed end leading chain travel as illustrated; lubricate the chain. Leave the sprocket cover off for the final nut check.
verification: Original sprocket and new lock washer seated; nut temporary only; new chain clip correctly oriented; shift pedal 12 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the engine ground and starter lead
steps.instruction: Restore head ground terminal at its illustrated location7Nm; exact routing permits its terminal to face either way, so retain original untensioned routing. Restore starter lead6Nm while holding motor-side nut and replace rubber terminal cover. Restore its clamps and lead path along cylinder without slack.
verification: Ground7Nm/starter6Nm; terminal supported during tightening; rubber cover/lead route restored.

steps.title: Reconnect and route the engine harness
steps.instruction: Reconnect labeled stator, crank-position, gear-position and coolant-temperature couplers/covers. Stator passes behind radiator without tension-arm pinch; gear lead follows case inside front engine bracket without slack. Clutch cable must not sag down; protector contacts radiator hose outside stator/gear leads. Regulator leads stay inside tension arm. Restore frame clip lock forward and trim where shown; starter lead follows cylinder without slack. Reproduce the exact left/right routing and tie positions, distinguishing trimmed ties from those the source says leave uncut.
verification: All identified engine couplers latched; cable/lead separation and exact ties restored; no inherited newer-year grommet arrangement.

steps.title: Reseat the throttle body
steps.instruction: Remove intake protection and seat the intact throttle body fully in its original engine-side joint. Restore the clamp orientation and tighten the throttle-body joint clamp to 3.0 N·m. Keep both cables routed without tension and check full smooth throttle return. Sensors and calibration screws remain untouched. Reconnect all three labeled injector/pressure/TPS couplers without moving sensors.
verification: Joint fully seated 3.0 N·m; throttle returns smoothly; cables not trapped.

steps.title: Lubricate the sliding and cable-end surfaces
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the throttle-grip sliding surface. Lightly grease the cable ends and inside of the grip as shown. Keep grease away from the exterior gripping surface and the brake.
verification: Sliding and cable-end contact surfaces lubricated.

steps.title: Reconnect pull and return cables
steps.instruction: Restore each identified cable end to its original seat and groove in the throttle tube. Place the rubber cover and slide the intact grip/tube onto the handlebar. Confirm both cable ends and their outer housings are seated correctly before closing the housing.
verification: Both cable ends seated in the correct positions without crossing.

steps.title: Secure the housing
steps.instruction: Fit the housing and tighten its screws to 3.8 Nm. Check grip movement immediately. If the housing causes binding, reposition and retighten it, then check again. Restore the housing cover and rubber cover.
verification: Housing torqued; grip moves smoothly and returns.

steps.title: Verify free play and return before starting
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, check free play and smooth full return through the steering travel. The retained setup must still have 3–6 mm free play and no binding. If not, correct seating/routing before starting; do not use a running engine to diagnose a bound throttle.
verification: Record 3–6 mm free play and full return at centre and both steering limits.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Remove temporary port covers. Restore radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 to their marked engine connections and original clamp positions; tighten each disturbed radiator-hose clamp screw to 1.5 N·m. Check there are no kinks or trapped hoses. Radiator pipe seals and temperature sensor were not removed.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 correct; disturbed clamps 1.5 N·m.

steps.title: Seat the new header gasket
steps.instruction: Install the new exhaust-port gasket at the cylinder head and refit header pipe 1. Tighten all header nuts first to 7 N·m, then retighten them to 10 N·m. Do not apply the protector-screw locking-agent note to these nuts.
verification: New exhaust-port gasket; all header nuts 7 then 10 Nm.

steps.title: Locate pipe 2 and its clamp
steps.instruction: Install new joint gaskets in the exact exploded locations. Refit clamp, pipe2 and bracket bolt. Engage clamp projection in pipe/silencer slot and keep clamp off the raised pipe projection. Leave final clamp/bracket torque until silencer is seated.
verification: New joint seals and clamp projection/slot alignment correct.

steps.title: Refit the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Refit the silencer clamp and complete silencer on the seated joint. Install the retained mounting hardware and tighten both silencer mounting bolts to 30 N·m.
verification: Both silencer mounts 30 N·m; joints fully engaged.

steps.title: Tighten the bracket and both clamps
steps.instruction: Confirm front and rear joints remain fully inserted while tightening the exhaust-pipe bracket bolt to 20 N·m, pipe-2 clamp bolt to 12 N·m and silencer clamp bolt to 12 N·m.
verification: Bracket 20 N·m; each joint clamp 12 N·m; projections correctly located.

steps.title: Restore the two suspension access joints
steps.instruction: With exhaust fully seated and torqued, align supported shock lower and connecting-arm frame joints with their retained collars/seals. Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the disturbed bolt circumference and threads. Insert connecting-arm frame bolt from RIGHT and shock lower bolt from LEFT. Tighten frame connecting-arm nut80Nm and shock lower nut53Nm. Inspect unobstructed movement and full seating; retain support until closure is verified.
verification: Correct bolt directions, M grease, frame80Nm and shock lower53Nm; no trapped seal or binding.

steps.title: Seat the case and secure its mounts
steps.instruction: Remove intake protection and seat complete aircase with retained ECU, coil and filter onto its original joint. Restore collars, dampers and washers; three case bolts7Nm and joint clamp3Nm. Reconnect labeled ECU, coil and intake-temperature couplers/covers. Restore sub-lead between ECU and case and clips fully against ribs; keep harness clear of rails/intake joint. Fully seat plug cap facing right within the illustrated10-degree range. ECU/coil mounts remain untouched.
verification: Three7Nm case bolts/3Nm clamp; case-mounted electronics connected and original orientation preserved; plug cap fully seated facing right.

steps.title: Verify the restored intake
steps.instruction: Check case support, fully seated intake joints, reconnects and retained ECU/coil mounts. Verify no temporary covers remain and no wire lies pinched under case or between frame rail and joint. Filter remains correctly seated.
verification: Sealed supported intake and retained electronics; all protection removed.

steps.title: Reconnect the fuel system
steps.instruction: Restore tank on its original four dampers and retained collars. Tighten two front mounts7Nm and rear retaining screw9Nm. Remove joint covers, press fuel joint until click and lock cover/holder. Reconnect white2-pin pump connector. Route BOTH fuel hose and pump lead through cover guide; keep pump lead outside hose, hose ahead of battery, with no pinch/kink.
verification: Tank7/9Nm at exact mounts; fuel joint clicked/locked; both hose and lead guided.

steps.title: Refill with the specified mixture
steps.instruction: Use the specified aluminum-compatible ethylene-glycol antifreeze and distilled water at a final 1:1 coolant-to-water ratio. Do not mix antifreeze types. Fill to the maximum level illustrated in PDF96. The complete system nominal volume is 1.03 L including all routes; correct level and concentration govern, not forcing in that amount after an incomplete drain. Wash any spill on paint away immediately with water.
verification: Mixture/product and amount recorded; level at illustrated maximum.

steps.title: Secure the radiator cap
steps.instruction: Install and secure the radiator cap. Account for the drain hardware, collection container and tools before running the engine.
verification: Cap secured; drain sealed; tools clear.

steps.title: Refill the oil for the actual engine condition
steps.instruction: Record applicable oil quantity:.63L unchanged filter,.65L filter removal,.90L disassembled engine. Use source-listed Yamalube/API SG-or-higher JASO MA with SAE10W40,10W50,15W40,20W40 or20W50 selected against the ambient-temperature chart. No additives. Record product and actual quantity, check filler cap/seal condition and install cap. Do not copy newer-year filler O-ring grease/replacement instructions absent here. Flow and exact final level checks remain required.
verification: Actual oil product and case-specific quantity recorded; cap secure; no unsupported filler torque/preparation.

steps.title: Reconnect the battery and inspect routing
steps.instruction: Recheck interfaces, reconnect positive before negative and restore positive cover. Both battery leads pass UNDER the crossmember; source permits either relative order. Negative lead coupler sits right of starter relay; restore battery bracket clips and protect all conductors from frame contact.
verification: Positive then negative; both under crossmember; covers/clips restored.

steps.title: Refit the panels and seat
steps.instruction: Fit air-scoop projections into aircase holes, grooves over ribs and remaining projections into slots; bolts7Nm. Refit aircase cover with its two rear slots engaging case edges and left/right ribs aligned with scoop projections; secure quick-fastener screw and restore fuel breather to cover as illustrated. Refit right-cover projections/slots with its rib under rear-fender rib. Slide seat forward and secure its two bolts22Nm; ordinary cover fasteners7Nm. Restore fuel-cap cover with attached plastic bands all the way under seat.
verification: Scoop/cover locators seated;22Nm seat and7Nm ordinary covers; cap-cover bands under seat; breather restored.

steps.title: Measure and adjust chain slack
steps.instruction: Loosen the rear axle nut and both adjuster locknuts first. With the rear wheel raised and gearbox in neutral, pull the chain upward above the chain-guide mounting bolt with about 50 N. Measure between the drive-chain guide and the bottom of the chain at the exact diagram location. Adjust both sides equally to 50–60 mm. Push the wheel forward so each puller/end plate is seated against the swingarm end.
verification: Measured slack 50–60 mm using OEM50 N reference; pullers equally adjusted and seated.

steps.title: Secure the rear axle and adjusters
steps.instruction: Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m and both chain-adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m. Recheck the chain slack after tightening.
verification: Axle 135 N·m; locknuts 21 N·m; final slack recorded.

steps.title: Lock the drive sprocket after rear-wheel closure
steps.instruction: With rear axle and adjusters torqued, chain installed and rear brake firm, keep neutral and have a helper hold the rear brake. Tighten the hand-fitted sprocket nut90Nm with a torque wrench. The exact2022 source gives no locking-agent preparation for this nut; do not inherit it from another year. Bend the new lock-washer tabs firmly against the nut flats. Restore the retained chain guide/bracket and cover at7Nm. No impact, heat or case jamming.

source_links.title: Nick Dole manual rear-brake holding technique

verification: Nut90Nm/new washer tabs locked; original guide/bracket restored; cover7Nm; brake holding load controlled.

steps.title: Accept the completed repair
steps.instruction: Record the actual top-end parts installed and the accepted cold timing, clearance, fit and refit records from the preceding steps. The bike remains fully cool and has not yet been started after repair. Perform the following filter/static checks and cold pressure-tester attachment before its first oil-flow start. Record verified exact oil-check-bolt fastening and seal closure before any engine start; unresolved closure prevents starting. Unresolved mechanical or lubrication-preparation faults remain open.
verification: Actual repair records and oil-check-bolt closure accepted; engine fully cool; first startup not yet performed.
steps.composition_adaptation: Replace standalone prior-start entry with the actual continuous-route cold pre-start state, preserving exact check-bolt closure.

steps.title: Choose the actual parts route
steps.instruction: New valves, piston, rings, camshaft or gears require about 30 minutes at no more than half throttle. A new cylinder or crankshaft requires about one hour: 20 minutes at no more than half throttle, inspect, then 40 minutes at no more than three-quarter throttle and inspect again. With both groups renewed, keep at or below half throttle for the first 30 minutes; this overlap is an explicit conservative workflow adaptation. Record the actual parts route.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Open filter access
steps.instruction: Lift the fuel-cap cover from its rear as shown, using both hands. Loosen the aircase-cover quick fastener; release both side ribs from scoop projections and slide the cover forward. Turn the two retaining plates in the diagram direction. Withdraw the air-filter guide and separate foam element, inner guide and seal without admitting dirt into the intake.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Clean and oil the foam
steps.instruction: Wash with air-filter cleaner or kerosene, squeeze without twisting and dry fully. Replace damaged foam. Work Yamaha or quality foam-filter oil evenly through the foam in a bag; wipe excess with a clean cloth. It must be wet throughout but not dripping. Do not use gasoline or the source-prohibited volatile cleaners.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Restore the sealed intake
steps.instruction: Fit seal and inner guide into the foam, then fit the foam to the air-filter guide. Grease the entire seal lips with lithium-soap grease. Engage both rear guide projections in the case slots and verify a continuous seal with no trapped, turned-up foam or gap. Rotate both retaining plates back. Engage the cover rear slots over case edges and align its side ribs with scoop projections; secure the quick fastener and restore breather routing. Restore the fuel-cap cover with its plastic bands fully beneath the seat.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Perform the pre-ride inspection
steps.instruction: Complete the pre-ride inspection: coolant/fuel/oil levels and no leaks; sequential shifts and smooth clutch; effective brakes; full throttle return and 3–6 mm free play; aligned lubricated chain; wheels/spokes/tires; smooth steering without play; smooth leak-free suspension; unrestricted cables and secure connectors. Cold tire pressure is 100 kPa (15 psi) front/rear. Correct failures before riding.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Restore fuel and verify readiness to start
steps.instruction: Lift fuel-cap cover and add clean recommended unleaded minimum91(R+M)/2 gasoline; E10 permitted. Secure cap and restore cover with bands under seat. Verify latched pump connector and fuel hose/holder and no fuel leak. Select neutral in a ventilated area before starter operation.
verification: Correct fuel/cap/cover; no leaks; neutral and ventilation.

steps.title: Attach the pressure tester while cold
steps.instruction: Use the Mityvac MV 4560 method only with confirmed correct radiator adapter fit. With the engine fully cool, remove the cap under a thick cloth, slowly vent at the detent, then remove after hissing stops. Fill coolant to the source upper level and inspect hoses. Wet the adapter seal with water or coolant, seat it in the filler neck and secure both hose compression connections. Keep the original cap off until testing and full cooling are finished.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Verify oil flow immediately at idle
steps.instruction: With fuel, intake, electrical and mounting closure complete and the correctly fitting pressure tester already attached cold, start at idle only. Observe the oil-check window for oil flow and decreasing level while monitoring the pressure gauge. If the oil level does not decrease, pressure rises rapidly toward the stated ceiling, or a leak/abnormal condition appears, stop immediately; do not rev to force oil flow. The following three-minute warm-up continues from this initial start.
verification: Initial idle oil flow and gauge behavior accepted; warm-up continues without a separate earlier start.
steps.composition_adaptation: Combine exact oil-flow startup with approved cold-attached tester monitoring; preserve both fault conditions.

steps.title: Warm with the gauge connected
steps.instruction: Monitor the connected gauge while warming for Yamaha’s three minutes. Stop for rapid pressure rise, abnormal gauge behavior, leaks or pressure approaching the 137.3 kPa ceiling. Do not pump above that ceiling. If stopped for a fault, let the system cool fully before releasing pressure or disconnecting; investigate before repeating. This sequence combines Mityvac cold attachment/engine-on monitoring with Yamaha’s head-gasket warm-up requirement.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Check cooling-system pressure
steps.instruction: After the three-minute warm-up, stop the engine and apply only enough pressure to reach 137.3 kPa (19.9 psi), never exceed it. Confirm it holds for 5–10 seconds. Check radiator/hose joints for leakage and hoses for bulging. A loss of pressure or visible defect requires correction and repeat testing; record actual pressure and hold time.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Cool fully before removing the tester
steps.instruction: Leave the connected equipment undisturbed until the engine is completely cool. Then use the MV 4560 relief lever to release remaining pressure before disconnecting under a cloth. Refill to the source level and refit the radiator cap. This cold-release restriction comes from Mityvac page 9; never remove a hot cap or hot pressurized adapter.
verification: Record the actual equipment, condition and test result; unresolved faults remain pending.

steps.title: Warm for the operating checks
steps.instruction: After the test equipment has been removed with the engine fully cold, coolant restored and radiator cap secured, restart and warm the engine for the following measured operating checks. Keep the cap closed; stop for abnormal oil flow, leakage or noise.
verification: Pressure-test equipment removed cold; cap restored before measured operating checks.
steps.composition_adaptation: Prevent access warm-up from preceding cold pressure-test closure.

steps.title: Check the warm idle
steps.instruction: Use the correctly configured YDT 90890-03269 (US USB) or 90890-03264 to confirm coolant at 70–80 °C. Measure speed with tachometer 90890-06760 or YU-39951-B, connected as shown to the ignition-coil high-tension lead. With the starter knob fully returned and normal filter/compression/free play, verify 1900–2100 r/min. If necessary, adjust the idle screw; clockwise raises speed.
verification: Record temperature and accepted idle speed.

steps.title: Set the final grip free play
steps.instruction: Stop the engine. If final adjustment is needed after idle setting, loosen the grip adjuster locknut, turn the adjuster to obtain 3–6 mm free play, and tighten the locknut. Confirm smooth full return again.
verification: Record final 3–6 mm free play and secure locknut.

steps.title: Verify idle through steering travel
steps.instruction: Restart the warm engine without starter enrichment. Turn the handlebar fully left and right: idle must not change. If it changes, stop and correct cable routing/seating or adjustment before repeating this check. Hold the engine-stop switch until the engine fully stops when the check is finished.
verification: Record unchanged idle across steering travel; engine stopped.

steps.title: Allow complete cooling
steps.instruction: After the operating check has stopped the engine, let it cool completely before opening the radiator cap for the next cold-level check.
verification: Engine stopped and fully cooled before the cap is opened.

steps.title: Recheck the cold level
steps.instruction: Keep the bike upright on level ground. With the engine cooled, use the cloth and slow pressure-release method to remove the cap. Allow the coolant to settle, check against the illustrated maximum and add the correct mixture if low. Restore the cap securely. A leak or repeatedly dropping level requires repair rather than repeated top-offs.
verification: Final cold level and mixture recorded; cap secured; no unresolved loss.

steps.title: Verify the installed engine and record closure
steps.instruction: Follow exact oil-level method upright on level ground: warm2-3minutes, stop and wait about1minute. Verify oil above the minimum window mark. Place a container, remove the identified level-check bolt and verify oil does not run out; if it does, drain excess until last drop. If at/below minimum, add correct oil above minimum and repeat exact check. Restore check bolt/seal using the documented exact-interface closure obtained before work; record source, actual torque and seal action. Do not restart or return to use with this closure unresolved. Check leaks, clutch7-12mm, throttle3-6mm/full return, brakes firm, chain50-60mm and recorded warm steering idle. Record mount/fluid/support closure and any separate bench record.
verification: Actual final level and documented check-bolt closure recorded; all fluid/chain/control/support checks complete; no unresolved leak/binding.

steps.title: Ride the first interval
steps.instruction: Warm the fully assembled engine using its accepted starting procedure. In a controlled off-road area, ride about 20 minutes at no more than half throttle. Stop immediately for a problem and record actual riding time/symptoms. Automatic stop after 7 minutes idling does not make idling into riding time.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Stop and inspect
steps.instruction: Check mounted areas for looseness and oil or other leaks. Resolve any problem before continuing. Record actual findings; a symptom-free interval does not complete post-break-in maintenance.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Complete the recorded parts route
steps.instruction: For valves/piston/rings/camshaft/gears without cylinder or crankshaft replacement, ride about 10 further minutes at no more than half throttle. For a new cylinder or crankshaft, ride about 40 further minutes; with new valves/piston/rings/camshaft/gears too, retain half throttle for the first 10 minutes, then never exceed three-quarter throttle. Stop for abnormal behavior and record actual time and throttle ceiling.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Inspect before maintenance
steps.instruction: Stop and thoroughly inspect mounted areas and leakage, cable stretch, brake action/free play, chain stretch and loose spokes. The riding period is complete only for the recorded parts route; maintenance below remains unfinished.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Drain and inspect the used oil
steps.instruction: Upright on level ground, warm the engine several minutes, stop and wait about five minutes. Place a clean container under the single drain. Remove filler cap and drain bolt with gasket; drain the oil. Inspect for dirt and foreign material, especially metal chips. If present, stop: Yamaha requires crankcase disassembly and inspection before proceeding.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Renew the oil filter
steps.instruction: Renew the oil filter during this oil change. Remove cover and old filter. Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the new cover O-ring from diagram234, install it, and fit the exact new filter in diagram90 orientation. Refit cover bolts10Nm. Filter renewal is included in this route; the post-break-in list itself requires the oil change.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Expose the generator mounting check
steps.instruction: With oil drained, first remove the fuel-cap cover because its plastic band couples it to the seat. Remove the left side cover, seat, aircase cover and left air scoop. Label and disconnect stator and crank-position couplers. Remove shift pedal, preserving punch-mark alignment. Record the lead holders retained with the left-cover hardware; keep the engine installed.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Open the left cover only
steps.instruction: Release cover fasteners progressively and lift the cover without pulling wires. Retain both dowels and external lead holders; discard the gasket. Keep stator, internal holder and sealed grommet attached to the cover and rotor attached to the shaft. Secure assemblies do not require removal merely for a mounting inspection.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Inspect generator mounting
steps.instruction: Check generator rotor and stator mounted areas for looseness and visible contact damage, and inspect connectors. Keep sound mounted assemblies intact. Record the actual inspection. Loose or damaged assemblies require separate generator repair with correct taper/key, sealing and fastening steps; a blind torque check does not replace that repair.
verification: Record actual outcome; unresolved required work prevents completion.

steps.title: Reseal the left side
steps.instruction: Fit both dowels and a new left-cover gasket. Restore the cover and external lead holders in diagram225 and tighten cover bolts in stages and crisscross to10Nm. Preserve undisturbed grommet sealing and unpinched wires. Align pedal/shaft punch marks and tighten pedal bolt12Nm; reconnect both couplers and restore illustrated lead routing.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Close drains and refill
steps.instruction: Fit a new gasket and tighten the single drain bolt20Nm. Fill0.65L for this filter-removal service. Use Yamalube or oil meeting API SG or higher and JASO MA; listed SAE grades are10W-40,10W-50,15W-40,20W-40 or20W-50 selected for ambient conditions. Do not add chemical additives or admit dirt. Check retained filler cap and seal condition before installing. Record actual oil/product. The0.90L disassembled-engine capacity is not this service refill; flow and exact final level checks remain required.
steps.verification: Record actual completion of this step, correct illustrated orientation and stated fastening/closure; unresolved damage, leakage or required external work remains pending.

steps.title: Inspect the repaired engine
